description: Production settings. All dev features disabled, optimized for performance and security.

auth.description: Authentication provider to use. Currently supported: 'supabase' (default). Other values default to supabase.

database.description: Database provider to use. Currently supported: 'supabase' (default). Other values default to supabase.

analytics.description: Analytics exporter to use. Currently supported: 'sentry' (default). Handles analytics event buffering and dispatch.

errorProvider.description: Error tracking provider to use. Currently supported: 'sentry' (default). Handles exception capture, user identification, and breadcrumbs.

splashScreen.description: Show splash screen on app load (after bootstrap + 1s buffer)

debugLogs.description: Enable verbose debug logging throughout the app - helps diagnose production issues

loggerCategories.description: Configure which logger categories are enabled in production

consent.description: Default analytics consent level on first app launch. Options: 'none' (no tracking), 'basic' (GDPR minimum), 'full' (all tracking). Default 'basic' is privacy-first and GDPR-compliant.

buffer.description: Analytics event buffer configuration (offline queueing). maxSize: max events in queue. maxRetries: attempts before discard. batchSize: events per flush request. retryBaseMs: base exponential backoff (1s→2s→4s→8s→16s). debounceMs: debounce flush on network flaps. batchDelayMs: delay between batch sends (ms) to avoid overwhelming backend. endpoint: analytics backend URL (required for production; set via config or EXPO_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT). If null, derived from EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN (Sentry only).

breadcrumbs.description: Sentry breadcrumb queue configuration (offline persistence). enabled: queue breadcrumbs when offline. provider: Sentry adapter name. maxBreadcrumbs: max breadcrumbs in queue (FIFO overflow). batchSize: breadcrumbs per flush request. maxRetries: max retry attempts per breadcrumb (then discard). retryBaseMs: base exponential backoff (1s→2s→4s→8s→16s). debounceMs: debounce flush on network flaps (once per 5s). breadcrumbRetentionDays: discard breadcrumbs older than N days (don't waste quota).

dispatch.description: Event dispatch configuration. async: fire-and-forget (non-blocking). debounceMs: debounce dispatch requests (batch multiple events). queueSize: max pending dispatches before dropping. timeout: max time waiting for all exporters to respond.

performanceBaseline.description: Performance baseline tracking configuration. Enable/disable via featureFlags.track-performance-baseline. maxSamplesPerOp: max samples per operation (FIFO rolling window, prevents unbounded storage). warmupSamples: skip first N samples to prevent cold-start skew (e.g., 5). regressionThresholdPct: threshold for regression alert as % above p95 (e.g., 20%). percentileForCompare: which percentile to use for regression detection (e.g., 95).

exporters.description: Exporter enable/disable settings (feature flag control). Each exporter is independently configurable for runtime toggle without code changes.

backgroundJobs.description: Job queue configuration (production: conservative, stable timings)

circuitBreaker.description: Circuit breaker thresholds for API endpoints (production: conservative)

entitlements.description: Entitlement lifecycle and reminder configuration (production: stable defaults)

adaptivePayload.description: Adaptive payload sizing based on network quality (4G→2G). Enables compression, skips optional fields on slow networks, disables images/maps on very slow connections.

telemetry.description: Network telemetry sampling (healthCheck: 10%, errors: 50%, maxQueue: 1000 events)

network.description: Network connectivity detection settings (pingInterval: 10 minutes, debounce: 500ms to prevent flap spam)

ios.platformNotes: iOS constraints: typical devices are slower (A-series chips) and have limited RAM. Stricter slowScreen threshold (2000ms vs 3000ms base) detects jank earlier. More frequent health checks (60s vs 600s) for less stable cellular networks.

android.platformNotes: Android constraints: similar to iOS (variable hardware, less stable networks). Stricter threshold + frequent checks. Network timeout remains at base (5s) as it's platform-agnostic.

web.platformNotes: Web platform: modern browsers on desktop hardware are significantly faster. Looser thresholds (5000ms vs 3000ms base) reflect higher baseline performance. Network stack is more predictable; uses base intervals.

desktop.platformNotes: Desktop (Electron): between mobile and web. More powerful than typical phones but less optimized than web browsers. Thresholds split the difference (4000ms). Inherits all other base config.

offline.description: Offline queue configuration. maxQueueSize: max pending requests (FIFO). maxRetries: attempts per request before discard. retryIntervalMs: base retry interval (exponential backoff). circuitBreaker: fail-fast after N consecutive failures, reset after N ms. redactionEnabled: strip auth tokens from queued requests.

remoteConfig.description: Remote config sync settings. Clock skew tolerance: 60s (allows ±60s device clock drift before denying entitlements as fail-secure measure). Entitlement poll interval: 5 minutes.

safeMode.description: Safe mode health check configuration (production: conservative). Storage: 5m, Auth: 4h

compression.description: Cache compression middleware configuration (production: conservative 10% sampling, 1KB threshold)

cacheSecurityLimits.description: Hard security limits for cache growth (hardMaxBytes: 500MB, hardMaxEntries: 5000, rejectOversizedEntries: true = reject, false = warn)

cacheCapacity.description: LRU cache capacity management (production). hardMaxBytes: 10MB mobile, 50-100MB desktop. softThreshold: evict at 90% capacity. targetAfterEviction: target 70% after cleanup. Adjust per platform in platform-specific overrides.

featureFlags.description: Max ms to wait for remote flag sync before continuing startup with a fallback. Snapshots older than featureFlags.staleDays are treated as dead.

networkConditions.description: Timeout multipliers scale by network speed and type. Applied at runtime based on detected connection. Cellular connections are generally slower than WiFi equivalents.

kernel.description: Phase timeout base values (ms) + per-phase failure strategies. Shared across prod and dev. Effective timeout = baseMs * networkConditions[detectedSpeed]. Dev env overrides networkConditions multipliers for generous debugging; baseMs remains consistent. 'fail' = app crash; 'force-skip' = continue without phase; 'conditional-fail' = degrade + retry.
